method.timing_window: search_hybrid(k=20, depth=200, ef=600) round trip, identical on both sides of the speedup: same call, same rows. The baseline differs only by enable_indexscan/bitmapscan = off, which forces the vector CTE to an exact scan. Component variants time search_vector(k=200) and search_bm25(k=200) — the CTEs' workloads.
method.hardware: MacBook Air M1 8GB (fanless), podman VM 4 vCPU / 4GB
method.protocol: pg_prewarm; 520 queries; 1 warmup + 3 measured runs; four variants back to back inside each query's slot, order rotated; repetitions collapsed per query first

decomposition.reads_as: components are what each CTE's workload costs run alone; fusion_overhead is hybrid minus their sum, an UPPER bound on genuine fusion cost (Postgres may overlap the CTEs, and any sharing shows up here as a negative contribution)

defect.status: NOT REPORTABLE — the fused ratio is bracketed by two contaminations of opposite sign, neither sized. Kept rather than deleted, on the same rule as results_speedups.json's provenance_defect: a wrong published number gets corrected in place, not disappeared.

bias_high__baseline_inflated.mechanism: The baseline's only available lever is planner GUCs, and they are not selective to papers_embed_idx. enable_bitmapscan=off removes papers_fts_idx ENTIRELY (a GIN index is reachable only via a bitmap scan), and enable_indexscan=off removes papers_pkey from the final join. So 'hybrid without the HNSW index' is actually 'hybrid without the HNSW index, without the FTS index, and without the primary key' — three seq scans of a 276 MB heap in one statement, not one.
bias_high__baseline_inflated.consequence: hybrid_exact measured 567.6 ms where an additive model of the intended baseline (exact vector arm ~61-73 ms + shared remainder ~8-16 ms) predicts ~90 ms.

bias_low__candidate_handicapped.mechanism: The variant order is a cyclic rotation, VARIANTS[rot:] + VARIANTS[:rot], which PRESERVES every adjacency — rotation is not randomization. hybrid_hnsw therefore runs immediately after the 567 ms baseline in 3 of 4 query slots, on a buffer pool the baseline's scans just evicted (276 MB pulled through a 128 MB shared_buffers).

defect.why_a_reordering_fix_would_not_repair_it: The eviction bias acts BETWEEN executions and a seeded permutation removes it. The GUC bias acts WITHIN a single execution and no ordering scheme touches it. Re-running with a fixed permutation would return a still-contaminated number wearing a repair.
defect.what_is_reportable_instead: Per-arm paired ratios. The vector arm is clean because VECTOR_SQL has exactly one index option, so the GUC IS selective there: 3.8x [3.6, 3.9] at ef=600, 24.1x [23.3, 25.0] at ef=40 (results_paired_speedup.json). The bm25 arm's index is worth 30.8x on its own, stated separately. The FUSED end-to-end ratio has no instrument.
